reason: E1 shows low friction and wear for a different 2D HEA coating on steel at room temperature, supporting the general concept of 2D HEA self-lubrication, but provides no evidence for high-temperature behavior, CoCrFeNi substrates, or adaptive tribolayer formation across 25–800 °C. E2 discusses wear of uncoated CoCrFeMnNi in UHV and oxide-film effects, which does not directly support the proposed coating intervention or its mechanism. The key premises about high-temperature adaptability and substrate-specific performance are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: A 2D high-entropy coating can be deposited on a CoCrFeNi substrate.
The coating will delaminate/reorganize during sliding to form an adaptive, lubricious tribolayer.
This tribolayer will reduce friction and wear across 25–800 °C.
The mechanism is analogous to stress-induced self-lubrication in related HEA systems.
